terms.definition: A discrete capability exposed to the model via a structured input schema and a call() method, enabling the agent to act on the world (read files, run commands, etc.).
A child agent spawned by the parent via AgentTool, running in a forked or in-process context with its own isolated conversation and tool access.
An OS-level process fork used to run a subagent in isolated memory, preserving the parent's state while the child executes independently.
A Git worktree providing an isolated working directory and branch for parallel agent execution without interfering with the parent's checkout.
A durable unit of tracked work with status transitions, blocking relationships, and filesystem-based persistence, representing a subagent or background job.
A user-invocable or trigger-activated capability defined by Markdown frontmatter, providing specialized domain knowledge or workflow automation to the agent.
A user-typed command starting with '/' that is parsed and dispatched by the REPL, either as a prompt substitution or a callback function.
A deterministic lifecycle event handler (command, prompt, HTTP, agent, or function type) that executes before or after tool calls or session events.
A named operational mode (default, plan, acceptEdits, bypassPermissions, dontAsk, auto) that governs how tool-use authorization decisions are made.
A function that maps a bash command string to a risk band (safe, destructive, etc.) used by the permission system to decide automatic approval or denial.
The process of reducing context length by summarizing or pruning conversation history, triggered when token budgets are approached.
A lightweight compaction pass that removes verbose tool outputs and redundant content from recent messages without full summarization.
A severe compaction event that aggressively prunes conversation history when token limits are critically exceeded, potentially losing detail.
An automatic compaction trigger that fires when the conversation approaches the model's context window limit, without user intervention.
A persistent knowledge entry stored in memdir, carrying type, age, and relevance metadata, surfaced during query context assembly.
The on-disk tiered memory system using MEMORY.md index and per-memory .md files, providing long-term knowledge persistence across sessions.
A single invocation of the agent from startup to shutdown, persisted as JSONL, with its own conversation history, state, and task tracking.
A read-only operational mode where the agent explores and produces a plan before switching to execution, enforced by tool-gating restrictions.
The engineering layer that wraps a language model, providing tool dispatch, state management, permission enforcement, and lifecycle control.
An observability hook that monitors agent behavior (cost, token usage, loop count) and can trigger back-pressure or shutdown decisions.
A runtime constraint or instruction that shapes agent behavior, such as CLAUDE.md rules, system prompt fragments, or hook-enforced policies.
A mechanism that slows or halts the agent when resource limits (tokens, cost, time) are approached, preventing runaway execution.
A tool that is not loaded into the model's tool list initially but is discovered on demand via ToolSearch, reducing prompt size for large tool catalogs.
A meta-tool that allows the model to discover and load deferred tools at runtime, implementing progressive tool expansion.
A hook event fired before a tool's call() method executes, allowing interception, modification, or denial of the tool invocation.
A hook event fired after a tool's call() method completes, allowing post-processing, logging, or side-effect enforcement.
A JSON file (manifest.json) that defines the book's structure: chapter metadata, source files, HER references, word targets, and audit pass counts.
A multi-agent pattern where one agent generates content and another evaluates it, used for quality assurance and iterative refinement.
The ability to snapshot and restore agent state (session, files, git) for rollback after failed operations, related to worktree isolation.
A cost-reduction technique that removes or summarizes verbose tool outputs from the model's context while preserving the fact of their execution.
